# Rule 6 — Escalation and conflict
Conflict should escalate naturally and give other players a chance to react. Do not jump straight to lethal violence over minor insults, harmless pranks, small thefts, or first-time arguments.
Use force that makes sense for the situation. Verbal warnings, reporting to security, non-lethal tools, restraint, or leaving the area should usually come before serious injury or killing.
Killing, spacing, gibbing, permanent confinement, or destroying someone’s body should only happen when the situation reasonably justifies it, such as direct lethal danger, confirmed hostile action, valid antagonist objectives, or a clear roleplay situation where all involved parties consent.
Roleplay-motivated killing or gibbing may be allowed when it has proper buildup, makes sense in-character, and all directly involved players are okay with it. Consent does not allow you to disrupt unrelated players, abuse mechanics, or ignore other rules.
Revenge should stay proportional. Being annoyed, embarrassed, lightly harmed, or inconvenienced does not give you permission to murder or ruin someone’s round.
